name: TPS562202SDRLR
title: 4.3 V to 17 V input, 2 A synchronous step-down converter with ECO mode, SOT563
summary: TPS562202S, a synchronous step-down converter for 2 A, has both power MOSFETs inside (140 mΩ high side, 84 mΩ low side), running from 4.3 V to 17 V and regulating 0.804 V to 7 V through a resistor divider on FB. Its D-CAP2 adaptive on-time loop needs no compensation parts and works with ceramic or polymer output capacitors; at light load it drops into ECO mode, a discontinuous mode whose switching frequency falls with load. It switches at about 580 kHz, soft-starts in a fixed 1.2 ms, and has valley current limiting, hiccup undervoltage protection, UVLO and thermal shutdown. The package is a 1.6 mm × 1.6 mm 6-pin SOT563 (DRL).
key_figures: 804 mV typ, 792 mV to 816 mV at 25 °C

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node, the junction of the high-side and low-side N-channel MOSFETs; the inductor's input end.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground for the control circuit and source of the low-side MOSFET. The feedback divider's ground returns to this pin at one point.

pins.name: BST
pins.function: Supply for the high-side gate driver; a 0.1 µF capacitor goes from BST to SW.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable, active high. The pin must be pulled up for the converter to run; it has an internal resistance to GND of 400 kΩ typ.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input, taken from the output through a resistor divider.

circuits.title: 1.05 V, 2 A reference design
circuits.description: Steps an input of 4.3 V to 17 V down to 1.05 V at up to 2 A. C1 and C2 (10 µF each) and C3 (0.1 µF) decouple VIN to ground. The switch node drives L1, 2.2 µH, into the output bank C8 and C9, 22 µF each. C7, 0.1 µF from BST to SW, feeds the high-side gate driver. R1 (3 kΩ) and R2 (10 kΩ) divide the output down to the 0.804 V the FB pin regulates; C4, across R1, is not installed. R3, 10 kΩ, connects EN to VIN.

operation.text: D-CAP2 is an adaptive on-time scheme with compensation inside the part. Each cycle starts with the high-side MOSFET on; a one-shot timer ends the on-time, and that time scales with VIN and inversely with VOUT so the frequency stays nearly constant across input voltage. A new cycle starts when FB drops below the reference. An internal ramp added to the reference stands in for output ripple, so no ESR-generated ripple is needed and the loop is stable with ceramic or polymer capacitors and next to no output ripple.

As load falls, the valley of the inductor current reaches zero, the edge between continuous and discontinuous conduction. The low-side MOSFET then turns off at zero inductor current. The on-time stays about the same as in continuous mode, so the output capacitor takes longer to discharge to the reference and the switching frequency falls in proportion to load, keeping light-load efficiency high. Between pulses the part sleeps until FB falls below the reference. The transition current is given by the light-load equation. TPS562207S runs forced continuous conduction instead.

When EN goes high an internal soft start ramps the reference fed to the PWM comparator over 1.2 ms. If the output already holds a voltage, switching begins only once the rising internal reference passes the feedback voltage, so a pre-biased output ramps smoothly into regulation.

Current is limited on the inductor valley, cycle by cycle, by sensing the low-side MOSFET's drain-to-source voltage while it conducts; the sensing is temperature compensated. If the current is above the limit the low-side MOSFET stays on and the next on-pulse is held off until the current falls to the limit; following on-times are fixed. Because the valley is limited, the load current at the limit is the threshold plus half the inductor ripple. If the output then sags until FB crosses the UVP threshold, the part stops once the UVP delay has passed (24 µs typ) and restarts after the hiccup time (18 ms typ). The output returns to regulation once the overload goes away.
UVLO watches the internal regulator voltage and turns the part off when it is below threshold. It does not latch. VIN wake-up is 4.0 V typ (4.3 V max) and shutdown 3.6 V typ (3.3 V min).
Above about 160 °C junction temperature the part turns off, and it resumes once the temperature is back below about 135 °C. The protection does not latch.
With VIN over its UVLO threshold and EN above its threshold the converter switches normally; at heavy load in continuous conduction it runs at a nearly fixed 580 kHz.

At low frequency the divider and the internal gain set the loop gain, with 180° phase. Past the LC double pole the gain falls at –40 dB/decade while the phase drops fast; D-CAP2 contributes a zero at high frequency, which brings the slope back to –20 dB/decade and lifts the phase by 90° a decade above the zero. The LC pole has to sit below that zero but close enough to it for adequate phase margin; the recommended component values table meets this. Output capacitance of 20 µF to 110 µF is recommended, in ceramic or similar low-ESR types. Larger divider resistors improve very-light-load efficiency, but too large a value picks up noise and makes the FB input current error more visible.

The input needs a ceramic decoupling capacitor above 10 µF, with bulk capacitance added where the application needs it, plus 0.1 µF between pin 1 and ground for high-frequency filtering. Input capacitor voltage ratings must exceed the highest input voltage. A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor from BST to SW is required.
The input range is 4.3 V to 17 V, and the input must be above the output. The highest recommended duty cycle is 75 %, so the lowest recommended input is VO / 0.75.

Make VIN and GND traces as wide as possible, for low impedance and for heat spreading. Put the input and output capacitors as close to the part as possible and give them plenty of vias. Keep the SW trace short and wide to limit radiated noise. Do not route switching current under the part. Take the upper feedback resistor's connection from the output on its own trace, and return the feedback ground to the GND pin by a Kelvin connection. Route the feedback away from the switching node, ideally with a ground shield, and keep the FB node small. Make the ground run between the output capacitor and GND wide, for low impedance. In the example layout the input capacitor sits beside VIN and GND, the inductor and output capacitor beside SW, CBST beside BST, and the feedback resistors beside FB, with vias to a bottom-layer ground plane.
